findings.evidence: Lines 54–74 define `castLpₗᵢ`, `coeFn_castLpₗᵢ`, and `castLpₗᵢ_symm`, but no element-level application theorem; the analogous public `compMeasurePreservingₗᵢEquiv` API includes both `@[simp] ..._apply` and `@[simp] ..._symm_apply`.
findings.fix: Add an `@[simp] castLpₗᵢ_apply` equating application to the existing transport `cast`; the existing `castLpₗᵢ_symm` then supplies the inverse form.
findings.issue: `castLpₗᵢ` has only a pointwise coercion lemma, so consumers cannot rewrite the resulting `Lp` element itself without an extensionality proof.

findings.evidence: The declarations at lines 159, 176, and 185 orient compound transport expressions toward the canonical named mode/basis and do not form a loop; the underlying `HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ_apply`, `mapₗᵢ_refl`, and `mapₗᵢ_trans` normal forms are all `@[simp]`.
findings.issue: The direct computational normal forms for the new isometry and transported bases are not `@[simp]`, so routine simplification cannot identify a transported mode or basis.

summary: The new isometries have incomplete rewriting APIs: the general cast lacks an element-level application lemma, and the specialized normal-form equalities are not registered for simplification.
